text: Thereupon he laid himself down and fell asleep under a broom-brush. An angel of God touched him there and spoke to him: “Sit up so that you may eat!”

Michael, the great angel-prince of Israel, revealed this mystery to Elijah on Mount Carmel: The end and the age which shall come at the end of days, at the end of the four world-kingdoms, during the time of the reign of the fourth king who will arise.
The Spirit of YHWH lifted me on high and led me to the south of the world; there I saw an elevated place blazing in fire where no being could enter.
Again the Spirit lifted me on high and led me to the east of the world; there I saw how stars fought unceasingly with one another.
Again the Spirit lifted me on high and led me to the west of the world; there I saw how souls suffered judgment in great pain, each according to its works.

At that time Michael revealed to me: “The end which will come at the end of days during the time of the reign of a king who will arise, who bears the name Harmelat,” but some have said that he shall be called Tarmyla. Rabbi Simai has said, “he shall be called Hakhshart.” Rabbi Eleazar has said, “he shall be called Artaxerxes.” Rabbi Juda ben Betira has said, “he shall be called Cyrus.” Rabbi Shimon b. Yohai has said, “he shall be called Khusrau.” The correct name, as Rabbi Shimon ruled, is, as he said, “he shall be called Khusrau.”

A last king of Persia will engage in war against the Roman kingdom for three consecutive years; finally he will spread himself out therein twelve months long. And three war heroes will go out against him from the sea; but they will be handed over into the power of the lowest among kings, the son of a slave, who bears the name Gigit, and will fight against him from the sea. And such will be his marks, as Daniel saw him: His face is long; between his eyes he has no hair; and he is very tall; and his feet are long; and his lower legs are thin. And at that time he will stretch out his hand against the faithful people and at that time he will arouse three conflicts.

And all the stars shall gather themselves together and make their way to one place to seize houses and rob fields, and confound the orphans and widows alms in the street market. But when they repent, forgiveness will be theirs.
On the twentieth of Marheshvan the world will tremble and heaven and earth shake.

On the twentieth of Kislev all of Israel will pray and call for help before their Father in heaven. And on that day a sword shall descend and fall among the heathen, as it is written: “The sword devours this one as well as the other.” (2 Samuel 11:25)

On the twenty-second of Nisan the first of the exiles, numbering 18,000 men and women, will depart from Babylon. No casualties will be suffered by them. On the twenty-fifth of Tishri the second group of the exiles, numbering 17,000, will depart and find itself at the river Sambatyon. Twenty men and fifteen women among them will be killed. On the twenty-fifth of the eighth month the third group of exiles will depart; they will weep and lament for their slain brethren; they will lament forty-five days long in the desert, during which time they will neither eat nor drink, and their lives will be preserved by that which proceeds from the mouth of YHWH. Before the first group of exiles departs from Babylon, the second will have reached Babylon; as it is said: “Writhe in pain to bring forth, O daughter of Zion,” etc. (Micah 4:10)

On the twentieth of Nisan the king will arise from the sea and devastate and shake the world and attack the Temple mount and reduce it to ashes. Cursed among women be the woman who bore him! This is the horn which Daniel saw. And on that day distress and war shall take place against Israel.

Demetrius the son of Poryphos and Anpholipos the son of Panphos will lead the second war with a retinue of 100,000 riders, 100,000 foot soldiers, and 100,000 in ships. The Messiah, whose name is Yinnon, will come on the twentieth of Elul; and on that day, from nine to ten hours, Gabriel will descend and kill 92,000 men. On the twentieth of Tebet will rage the third war from Mekketz and Qirtalos, engaging the retinue of all the provinces, an extremely large throng which will reach from the great plain of Jaffa to Ashkelon. And on the twentieth of Shebat the Messiah will come, and attacking angels will descend and kill the entire crowd and will leave no one alive.

At that time the Holy One, blessed be He, will speak to Abraham: “Your descendants will sink to the lowest level,” for it is said: “Deep beneath the ground will you speak.” (Isaiah 29:4) But they will thereafter be raised above all peoples, for it is said: “YHWH your God will raise you above all the peoples of the earth.” (Deuteronomy 28:1) Then shall all peoples come and throw themselves down before every one of Israel and lick the dust of their feet; for it is said: “Kings shall be your attendants.” (Isaiah 49:23)

On the twentieth of Adar the Messiah will come with a following of 30,000 faithful, for it is said: “Justice shall be the girdle of his loins.” (Isaiah 11:5) And when the heathen shall see this, one of each, with his horse, will immediately be crushed, for it is said: “Such shall be the plague with which YHWH will strike all the peoples,” etc. (Zechariah 14:12-15) At that time, the Holy One, blessed be He, will speak to the heathen: “Woe to you godless who live at the end of the four kingdoms, for you shall all be swept away from the earth.”

Then one bushel of wheat shall yield 900 bushels; and in like manner will it be with wine and oil; and tree after tree will be weighted down with exquisite fruits, for it is said: “Let your branches shoot out, O Israel,” etc. (Ezekiel 36:8) And Israel will eat and rejoice for forty years.

Thereafter Gog and Magog will muster their warrior throngs; then all the heathen will assemble together and throng around Jerusalem for war. But the Holy One, blessed be He, will draw near and move against them. And the Messiah will come, while the Holy One, blessed be He, will stand at his assistance to wage war against them, for it is said: “YHWH will go out and dispute against the peoples as he once disputed on the day of battle.” (Zechariah 14:3) On that day the mountains will shake and the hills will tremble, and the walls and towers will collapse. And the Holy One, blessed be He, will gather together all the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth to devour their flesh and drink of their blood, for it is said: “The birds of prey will remain in summer by you and all animals of the earth will spend the winter there.” (Isaiah 18:6) And Israel will warm themselves with their weapons for seven years, for it is said: “The inhabitants of the cities of Israel will warm and heat themselves seven years with their armaments,” etc. (Ezekiel 39:9) And accordingly: “And the house of Israel will bury them for seven months in order to purify the land.” (Ezekiel 39:12)

And the following cities will be devastated: Jericho, Beirut, Beth-Horon, Siserin, Milkah, Arad, Shallum, Samaria, Beth-Migdol, Tyre, Beth-Halsawet, Lydda, Buz, Beth-‘Aynam, Hamat-Sefar, Hadashah, Antioch, Alexandria, and Edom. But all the Israelite cities will be encompassed by fire and angels of fire, for it is said: “But I will surround you with a wall of fire; this is the word of YHWH.” (Zechariah 2:9)

Then the last day will begin, which will last forty days. Then the mountains and hills will sway and shudder, and the earth will bring accusation against the godless, saying, “Somewhere someone killed someone”; for it is said: “The earth will reveal your blood,” etc. (Isaiah 26:21)

Elijah spoke: “I see how the dust of drowned dead men re-gathered, assuming the form they originally possessed in order to give praise to God, for it is said: ‘Recognize now that I, I am he’ (Deuteronomy 32:39) And also according to Ezekiel: ‘And I saw how tendons came on them’ (Ezekiel 37:8) And the ministering angels opened their graves and placed breath in their souls, and placed them on their feet.

And each one who was found guilty by the court, they pushed into a large battle field 2,000 cubits long and 50 cubits wide. And the eyes of the saints will gloat over the overthrow of those who have not longed after the Torah of the Holy One, blessed be He, for it is said: ‘They shall go out and look at the corpses of the men who rebel against me.’” (Isaiah 66:24)

Elijah spoke: “I see how fire and sulfur poured down from heaven on the godless, for it is said: ‘He rained coals on the godless.’ (Psalm 11:6) And the Holy One, blessed be He, will move the Holy Place far away from the place of eternal judgment, so that the saints hear not the cries of the godless and plead not mercy for them; and they shall become as if they had never been.”

Elijah spoke: “I see how Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the saints sit there; and the land before them is sown with every manner of delicacy; and that tree which the Holy One, blessed be He, has prepared, stands in the middle of the garden, as it is said: ‘But on the river, on both of its banks, all manner of trees will grow with edible fruits; whose leaves shall not fade and whose fruit will not fade’ (Ezekiel 47:12) And ships go from En Gedi to En Eglayim, loaded with cargo and provisions for the saints.”

Elijah spoke: “I see how a beautiful and glorious city, built, descended from heaven, for it is said: ‘Jerusalem, you rebuilt as a city, joined well together,’ (Psalm 122:3) built and completed; in the midst thereof are 3,000 towers, and the distance between each tower was 20 ris; and between each ris will be 25,000 cubits of emeralds and precious stones and pearls, for it is said: ‘Your windows will I make out of jasper.’” (Isaiah 54:12)

Elijah spoke: “I see saints in the thresholds of their erected houses and gates; and their portals are of precious stones; and the treasure houses of the temple are opened wide; in the midst thereof lawfulness and peace rule, for it is said: ‘And all your sons will be taught of YHWH.’ (Isaiah 54:13) And also: “Great good will be to them who have love for your law.” (Psalm 119:165) And also: ‘How great is your goodness which you have stored up for those who fear you.’” (Psalm 31:20) The Book of Elijah, of blessed memory, is ended.
